reports.game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
reports.title: Around 30 FPS after shader compilation. Occasional freezes and intro audio desync. First dungeon completed.
reports.what_happened:
Launch and intro:
The game launches successfully. The intro runs reasonably well, although there are some freezes and noticeable audio desynchronization: the audio finishes before the video does.
Shader compilation and performance:
Initial shader compilation takes some time and causes significant FPS drops during gameplay. Once more shaders have been compiled, performance settles at around 30 FPS. Some actions still cause brief freezes when performed for the first time, which appear to be related to shader compilation. Performance became more stable as I explored Kokiri Forest.
Gameplay progression:
I collected the sword and shield, then went to the Great Deku Tree. The dungeon was playable throughout my test, with no major issues apart from occasional freezes. I was able to defeat the boss and return to Kokiri Forest. This is where I ended my testing; I have not tested further progression.
Improvement compared with earlier builds:
Before build 95, I could not get into the game at all and only saw a black screen. Going from that to being able to complete the first dungeon is an incredible improvement.
Overall:
The opening section is playable, although initial shader compilation stutter and intro audio synchronization still need improvement. Performance becomes noticeably more stable as shaders are cached.

reports.title: Purple Horizontal Halo Around Distant Mountains and Hyrule Castle
reports.what_happened:
A noticeable purple/magenta horizontal halo appears along the upper edges of distant mountains and around Hyrule Castle when viewed from across Hyrule Field.
The issue is particularly noticeable when standing near the entrance to Kokiri Forest and looking towards Hyrule Castle.
I have also tested this by walking across Hyrule Field towards the castle. As I approach the castle, the purple halo remains visible for most of the journey. However, when I get very close to the castle, on its left side, just before jumping into the water and swimming underneath the drawbridge, I can clearly observe the halo gradually fading away until it completely disappears.
This gradual disappearance seems to indicate that the artifact is related to distance-based rendering rather than being a permanent texture issue.
Additional observations:
The purple/magenta artifact follows the upper outline of distant mountains and structures.
It is especially noticeable when looking towards Hyrule Castle from a distance.
It gradually fades as the camera gets closer to the affected objects.
It completely disappears when getting very close to the castle, near the water entrance underneath the drawbridge.
The issue could potentially be related to atmospheric fog, distance-based rendering, depth calculations, or shader handling, although the exact cause is unknown.

reports.title: Lichii Build 93 – Significant AMD Progress, but Lighting Flickering and Performance Issues Remain
reports.what_happened:
I wanted to share some positive feedback and report the remaining issues with Lichii NX2 Build 93 (09b78bd) while testing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition.
System specifications:
CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X
GPU: AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT
OS: Windows 11
Graphics API: Vulkan
GPU Accuracy: Fast
Mode: Docked
Resolution: 1X
Game update: 1.1.1
Improvements observed:
Compared to Build 88, Build 93 shows significant progress on my AMD GPU.
Previously, the game would get stuck compiling shaders or display a black screen. With Build 93, I was able to:
Complete the initial shader compilation and reach the main menu.
Play through the opening cinematics.
Successfully render the 3D environment.
Reach Kokiri Forest and control Link during actual gameplay.
Save the game, restart the emulator, and successfully load the saved game using Continue.
Reload approximately 1,375 cached shaders on the second launch.
Remaining issues:
Severe lighting flickering: Lights, glow effects, and certain environmental elements constantly flash or flicker during gameplay.
Incorrect lighting and overexposure: Some lighting effects appear excessively bright or visually corrupted.
Performance: Gameplay reaches approximately 24 FPS in Kokiri Forest, while menus and some cinematics run at approximately 30 FPS. Some sequences experience significant slowdowns.
Audio synchronization: Audio becomes noticeably desynchronized during cinematics.
Shader compilation: Initial shader compilation takes a considerable amount of time.
The lighting issues persist even after restarting the emulator and loading the cached shaders.
Conclusion:
Build 93 is a major improvement for my AMD RX 6900 XT. For the first time with Lichii on this GPU, I can reach actual 3D gameplay instead of getting stuck on a black screen.
However, the lighting flickering, graphical artifacts, and performance issues still prevent a smooth gameplay experience.
Thank you to the developers for the AMD and Vulkan fixes. The progress between Build 88 and Build 93 is very noticeable, and I hope these results help with further debugging and optimization.
I can provide gameplay recordings or logs if needed.

Failed: Severe visual and rendering glitches, plus cutscene desync issues:

The video appears to lag behind at a lower frame rate while the audio runs faster, causing the audio to finish long before the video ends. Distant Textures & Shadows: Distance textures fail to load proper lighting/shadows and remain dark until Link approaches.
Water Rendering: Water bodies appear completely solid black at medium to long distances.
Screen Artifacts: A persistent, neon-pink jagged boundary line stays locked at the top of the viewport frame.
Extreme Lighting Overexposure: Extreme bloom/overexposure occurs near and inside Kokiri Forest—especially when transitioning from Kokiri Forest to Hyrule—blinding the screen entirely white.
Shader Stuttering & Flashing: Sudden white texture flashes occur briefly whenever new shaders build/compile.
Zone Lighting Blackouts: Entering specific map zones triggers full environmental blackouts where everything except Link's model turns completely black.

reports.game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
reports.title: Playable to a certain degree
reports.what_happened:
Generally, everything kind of works. Controlling Link feels fine, and his moveset works as expected. The Menus render correctly, fonts and icons work.
However, performance is still rough. The game runs like absolute mega super dogshit, with noticeable stuttering and inconsistent frame pacing. In some areas like the inside of the Deku Tree, it is playable, but in others the FPS drops hard enough to make it feel like ass.
The bigger issue for me is the visuals. The game looks way too bright and washed out, almost like the HDR/tone mapping or exposure handling is wrong. Everything has this overly white, blown-out look, and it makes the game genuinely ugly compared with how it should look. Lighting also seems off in places, with haze and shadows not rendering correctly.
